bundle.guidance:
# Data Dashboard

An operational surface for analysts and on-call operators. Dark by default
because it lives on a wall display or a second monitor all day. Read at a
glance; drill in only when something looks wrong.

## Principles

1. **Answer "is anything wrong?" in two seconds.** Status and deltas first,
   detail below. A viewer who must read to find the problem has a broken
   dashboard.
2. **Density with air.** Compact type and tight rows, but never a tile
   touching another tile. The grid gap is the only separator; avoid borders
   inside a tile.
3. **Numbers are monospace.** Tabular figures so a column of values aligns and
   a changing value does not jitter.

## Layout grid

A responsive grid of tiles: `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(13rem, 1fr))` with
`--space-md` gaps. KPI tiles occupy one cell; a chart panel spans two or the
full row. Tables always come last. On a phone the grid collapses to one
column in the same source order, so put the most important tile first. Page
padding is `--space-lg`; do not cap the width — a dashboard uses the screen it
is given.

## Typography

Inter for labels, `--type-metric` (the monospace typography token) for every
headline figure. Labels are `--size-small`, uppercase, letter-spaced, in
`--color-text-secondary`. Headings never exceed `--size-h2`; on a dashboard a
big heading is wasted pixels.

## Colour usage

Near-black ground (`--color-bg-page`), tiles one step lighter
(`--color-bg-card`). Cyan (`--color-brand-primary`) is the interactive and
primary-series colour. Lime `ok`, amber `warn`, red `danger` for thresholds
only — a tile is coloured only when its value crosses one. Chart series follow
the palette in order and never repeat within one canvas. The `dark` mode is a
deeper, higher-contrast variant for wall displays in a dim room; both modes
must pass the same thresholds.

## Charts

Chart.js. Line for time series, bar for comparison across categories,
horizontal bar when category names are long. No pie or doughnut beyond a
single-value gauge. Always show the axis units, keep gridlines at
`--color-border-default`, and disable the legend when three or fewer series
can be labelled in the panel title.

## Diagrams

Mermaid `flowchart LR` for a pipeline overview panel, nothing else — a
dashboard that needs a sequence diagram is a document, not a dashboard.

## Components and when to use each

- `kpi-tile` — one metric, its delta and its threshold state. The top row of
  every dashboard.
- `chart-panel` — a titled canvas with a subtitle carrying the time window.
- `data-table` — compact rows for the long tail behind the tiles; right-align
  numbers, keep to eight visible rows and scroll.
- `status-dot` — inline health marker in a table row or a tile header.
- `filter-bar` — the time range and segment currently applied, printed as
  text so a screenshot stays self-explanatory.

## Do / don't

- **Do** print the time window on every panel; a screenshot outlives its
  context.
- **Do** show "no data" explicitly rather than an empty chart.
- **Don't** animate anything. Movement on a wall display reads as an alert.
- **Don't** put two units on one axis.
- **Don't** use a colour for a series that also means a threshold state.
